claim.claim-text: 1. A sterile staple implant kit that a surgeon may unpack and utilize during a surgery, comprising:

2. The sterile staple implant kit of claim 1, wherein the group of instruments comprises at least the staple inserter (100) and the surgical staple (116), the surgical staple being loaded into the staple inserter in a relaxed configuration of the surgical staple.

3. The sterile staple implant kit of claim 2, wherein the group of instruments comprises at least the staple inserter, the surgical staple, a bone drill (72), a drill guide (68), a locator pin (76), a tamp (80) and any of various surgical tools, such as drill sizers, forceps, staple removal tools, temporary pins, drill depth stops, fusion bone plates, bone plate fasteners, compression screws, and the like.

4. The sterile staple implant kit of claim 1, 2 or 3, wherein the staple inserter comprises a body (108) supporting a distal force applicator (112) that is mechanically coupled with a proximal handle (104), the distal forced applicator configured to distract the surgical staple when the proximal handle is rotated in a clockwise direction.

5. The sterile staple implant kit of claim 4, wherein rotation of the proximal handle moves a driver relative to a crown of the surgical staple, such that clockwise rotation of the proximal handle clasps the crown between the driver and a pair of grips (120,124) disposed within the distal force applicator, further clockwise rotation changing the surgical staple from a relaxed configuration to a distracted configuration suitable for implantation across a bone fusion or fixation site of a patient, and preferably wherein rotating the proximal handle counterclockwise allows the surgical staple to relax from being distracted.

6. The sterile staple implant kit of claim 5, wherein the pair of grips (120,124) comprises a first grip and a second grip, the first grip being disposed near a first leg of the surgical staple, and the second grip being disposed near a second leg of the surgical staple, the first and second grips being configured to engage the crown on the same side of the surgical staple.

7. The sterile staple implant kit of claim 4, wherein a staple retention clip (1280 is coupled with the distal force application to retain the surgical staple in a relaxed state during sterilization, packaging, and shipping, and preferably wherein the staple retention clip is configured to be removed from the distal force applicator during or after distracting the surgical staple prior to being implanted into a bone of a patient.

8. The sterile staple implant kit of any preceding claim, wherein the group of instruments includes a drill guide comprising a proximal handle (168) and a pair of parallel sleeves (172) configured to direct drilling of parallel holes across a bone fusion or fixation site of a patient, the positions of the parallel sleeves being substantially similar to a distance between a first leg and second leg of the surgical staple in a distracted configuration, and preferably wherein each of the parallel sleeves is configured to receive and guide a bone drill configured for drilling holes in human bone.

9. The sterile staple implant kit of claim 8, wherein the group of instruments comprises a locator pin (76) configured to be inserted through a first sleeve of the drill guide into a newly drilled hole in the bone of the patient during drilling of a second hole in the bone by way of the second sleeve of the drill guide.
10. A method for a sterile surgery-specific kit for use during performing a surgery, comprising:

11. The method of claim 10, wherein assembling comprises including at least a staple inserter and a surgical staple in the group of complementary instruments, and preferably wherein assembling further comprises loading the surgical staple in a relaxed configuration into the staple inserter, a staple retention clip being configured to retain the surgical staple coupled with the staple inserter.
